2026-11-15.title: Sunday of the Message to Zechariah
readings: A son for Abraham and Sarah
Do not fear, I am with you
The message to Zechariah in the Temple
2026-11-15.alt: First Sunday of the season of Annunciation (Suboro).
2026-11-15.verse: Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.
theo: The season of Suboro, the “good news”, opens not in Nazareth but in the Temple of Jerusalem, with an old priest burning incense. Zechariah and Elizabeth were “righteous before God”, yet they had no child, and they had grown old. God's first announcement in the New Testament is given to people who had prayed for years and seemed to have received no answer.

The Old Testament readings prepare us. Abraham and Sarah were given a son when it was humanly impossible; Abraham even laughed (Genesis 17:17). Hannah, barren and mocked, poured out her soul before the Lord in the sanctuary (1 Samuel 1:15) and became the mother of Samuel. Isaiah hears God say: “Do not fear, for I am with you.” The God of Israel brings life out of barrenness.

Zechariah's question is very human: “How will I know that this is so? For I am an old man.” He asks for a sign, and he receives one: silence until the promise is fulfilled. St Paul shows the opposite attitude in Abraham, who “hoping against hope… believed” and “grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God” (Romans 4:18, 20). Faith is not certainty that we can see; it is trust that God can do what he has promised.

John's mission is to go before the Lord “with the spirit and power of Elijah… to make ready a people prepared for the Lord” (Luke 1:17). Suboro is that preparation for us: a season in which the Church, like Zechariah in the Holy Place, waits, prays and lets God speak.
conn: Sarah (Isaac), Hannah (Samuel), the wife of Manoah (Samson) and Elizabeth (John): each birth shows that the future of God's people is God's gift, not human achievement.
Zechariah receives the message while the people pray outside at the hour of incense. In our Qurbono the incense rises with the prayers of the Church (Psalm 141:2; Revelation 8:3–4).
Malachi had promised that Elijah would come “to turn the hearts of parents to their children” (Malachi 4:5–6). The angel applies these words to John (Luke 1:17).
Ruth's “Where you go, I will go”.
Ruth's loyalty, a foreigner who becomes an ancestor of David and of Christ (Matthew 1:5), shows the faithful love that prepares the way of the Lord.
altar: Zechariah entered the sanctuary to offer incense; in every Holy Qurbono the priest does the same, and the people pray outside the veil as they did in the Temple. But we have more than Zechariah: the One whose coming he was promised now comes to the altar in his Body and Blood.
outline: Ask: have you ever prayed for something for years and thought God was not listening?
“Your prayer has been heard.” God's timing is not ours. Abraham, Hannah, Elizabeth.
His doubt is answered with silence, which becomes a school of faith. At the end his tongue is freed to praise (Luke 1:64).
Abraham's faith in Romans 4: trusting God when the facts say no.
John prepares hearts; Suboro prepares ours. Practical: reconciliation in families (“the hearts of parents to their children”).
“God has heard my prayer, even when I cannot see the answer.”
live: Write down one intention you have prayed for a long time, and offer it again at this Sunday's Qurbono.
Choose ten minutes of silence each day this week: no phone, no television, only God.
Take one step of reconciliation between parents and children in your family.
fathers: Commenting on Luke, he praises Zechariah and Elizabeth as righteous in both the priestly and the married life, and sees in John's birth a sign that God's grace surpasses nature (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke, Book 1).
He contrasts the priest who doubted with the Virgin who believed: the one who questioned was silenced, while she who believed conceived the Word (Commentary on the Diatessaron).
magis: St John the Baptist is the Lord's immediate precursor, sent to prepare his way; “prophet of the Most High”, he surpasses all the prophets.
Abraham is the model of the obedience of faith; “hoping against hope”, he believed, and so became the father of all who believe.
Abraham's faith is trust in a God who calls and promises, and who keeps his word even when it seems impossible.
saints: 16 Nov: St Matthew, Apostle (Malankara commemoration). 21 Nov: the Entrance of Mary, Mother of God, into the Temple. Confirm other commemorations in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-11-15.prayer: Lord God, you heard the prayer of Zechariah and Elizabeth and gave them a son to prepare the way of your Christ. Hear the prayers we have carried for so long, strengthen our faith when we cannot see, and make us a people prepared for the Lord. Amen.

quick: Suboro begins: the season of the good news.
God heard Zechariah's prayer late, but not too late.
Faith means trusting God's promise when we cannot yet see it.
2026-11-15.action: Offer again one long-standing intention at this Sunday's Qurbono.
2026-11-15.question: What prayer have I stopped praying because I thought God was not listening?
2026-11-15.special: First Sunday of Suboro, the season of Annunciation, in the Syro-Malankara liturgical year.
illus: A Kerala couple waited twelve years for a child, praying at every pilgrimage and novena. When a daughter was finally born, they named her Krupa, “grace”. Zechariah's story is told for every family that waits.

family.explain: Zechariah and Elizabeth prayed for a baby for many years. God heard them and gave them John. God hears our prayers too, even when we must wait.
family.intention: We pray for couples who are waiting for a child, and for all who are tired of waiting.
family.ask: Ask: “What are we waiting for God to do for our family?”

catechism: The prayer of Abraham: faith and waiting.
kidsaint: An old priest and his wife who loved God and kept his commandments. God gave them a son, John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Jesus. Lesson: never stop praying.
term: Syriac for “good news” or “annunciation”. The first season of the Syro-Malankara year, in which the Church meditates on the announcements of the coming of Christ, leading to Yaldo, the Nativity.
termMore: The season begins in the Temple, at the hour of incense. The New Testament opens where the Old Testament worship was offered, and moves towards the true Temple, Christ himself.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the season of Suboro begins, the season of good news. And where does the good news begin? In the Temple, with an old priest named Zechariah, burning incense while the people pray outside.

Zechariah and Elizabeth were good people. St Luke says they were “righteous before God”. And yet they had no child, and now they were old. How many years they must have prayed! And perhaps they had stopped asking. Then the angel says: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard.” God had not forgotten. God's answer came late, but not too late.

Zechariah could not believe it at once. “How will I know this? I am an old man.” And God gave him a strange sign: silence. For nine months he could not speak. That silence was a school. When John was born, the first thing Zechariah did with his freed tongue was to praise God.

Perhaps some of us here carry a prayer that God seems not to have answered: for a child, for a job, for a son who has gone away from the Church, for healing. Do not stop. Like Abraham, who “hoped against hope”, keep trusting. And use this season to prepare your heart, as John prepared a people for the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, do you like waiting? No! Waiting is hard. Zechariah and Elizabeth waited many, many years for a baby.
Then an angel came and said: “God has heard your prayer!” And God gave them a baby called John. John grew up to tell everyone: “Jesus is coming!”
When you pray, God always listens. Sometimes we must wait. Let's say together: “God hears my prayer!”

intro: Theme: “God hears our prayers, even when we have stopped hoping.”
The season of announcements begins with an old priest and his wife who had prayed for years for a child. Their story is the story of every family that waits, prays and is tempted to give up.

sub: Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous and blameless, yet childless: holiness does not exempt us from sorrow.
Like Hannah in the Temple, they poured out their soul before the Lord year after year.
Faithfulness in waiting is itself a gift that God sees and honours.
q: I am a woman deeply troubled; I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.
Both of them were righteous before God, living blamelessly according to all the commandments and regulations of the Lord. But they had no children.
points.apply: Bring to God again the prayer you have almost stopped praying.

sub: Abraham laughed at the promise of a son in old age; Zechariah asked for a sign.
God's “yes” came in the Temple, at the hour of incense, in the middle of ordinary duty.
Zechariah's silence was not only punishment but a school: nine months of listening before he could speak again.
q: Then Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?”
Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.
points.apply: Do your daily duties faithfully; God often speaks in the middle of them.

points.h: Preparing a people for the Lord
sub: John will turn hearts of parents to their children and make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
Like Ruth's loyalty, true faith commits itself: “your God shall be my God.”
This season asks each family to become a place where the Lord is expected.
q: Do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you.
With the spirit and power of Elijah he will go before him, to turn the hearts of parents to their children … to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
points.apply: Restore family prayer this week, even for ten minutes each evening.

concl: The God who heard Zechariah hears us. His timing is not ours, but his promise does not fail.
Let us wait like Elizabeth, listen like Zechariah, and prepare our homes for the coming of the Lord.
2026-11-15.resolve: Each evening this week, pray for one couple waiting for a child or for one family in sorrow.
